- **`main` doesn't contain any merged PR.** It has only 3 commits, ending at `61fc71a` (08:54 today). - **The CSV export never landed.** PR #3 and PR #5 were both closed without merging.

In short, `main` has no invoice totals fix, no CSV export and no PR #6 tests. If you reset the sandbox on purpose, that's fine. If not, work is lost.

- **B**: upgrade CI to Node 24 and actions v5.
- **C**: redo the work missing from `main`: the invoice

The run passed, and nothing in it is urgent. There are two things worth acting on.

**Worth fixing**
1. **CI runs on Node 20, which reached end-of-life in April 2026.** `.github/workflows/checks.yml:10` pins `node-version: 20`. The last line of the log also warns that `actions/checkout@v4` and `actions/setup-node@v4` were built for Node 20 and are being forced onto Node 24. The fix is to move to Node 22 or 24 and bump both actions to v5.
2. **5 tests are marked "expected fail".** That's 32 passed plus 5 expected fail, out of 37. `main` has no such markers in `src/`, so the PR branch added them. This run tested PR #6, branch `jv/write-tests-for-every-function-in-src-in-h40ttv`, not `main`. If that PR marked broken behaviour as "expected to fail" instead of fixing it, the bugs stay hidden and CI stays green. I tried to check the branch, but it no longer exists on GitHub (deleted, or the PR was closed), so I can't confirm what those 5 tests cover.

**Harmless**
- The `punycode` and `url.parse()` deprecation warnings come from the setup-node action itself, not from your code.
- `npm ci` reported 0 vulnerabilities. The token is read-only, and credentials are removed when the job finishes.

**About the log itself**
- The timestamps are 13/10/2026 21:38 UTC, which is today, not last week. Check you pulled the run you meant.
- The paste contains the same run about seven times, with the last copy cut off. That's a copy-paste issue, not a CI problem.

I haven't created any tasks.

Open questions: none.

Should I queue a task to upgrade Node and the actions, and another to find out whether PR #6 merged with those 5 expected-fail tests?

This is an earlier run of the same PR #6, at 21:37:40 against 21:38:51 for the first log you sent. The two runs tested different commits on the PR branch:

| Run | PR commit | Invoice tests | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 21:37 (this log) | `00c7a35` | 12 | 34 passed (out of 34) |
| 21:38 (earlier log) | `26452b5` | 15 | 32 passed, 5 expected fail (37) |

**What's worrying:** the later commit added 3 invoice tests, but the number of passing tests fell from 34 to 32. So at least 2 tests that passed in the earlier run were relabelled "expected to fail" rather than fixed. That either covers up a regression introduced in that commit, or turns tests that worked into ones that can no longer catch anything. Either way CI shows green while the 5 expected-fail tests check nothing. I can't see which tests they are because the branch no longer exists on GitHub. I'll check whether that commit reached `main`.

- CI still uses Node 20, which is end-of-life, and `checkout@v4` / `setup-node@v4` still trigger the deprecation warning. An upgrade is worth doing.
- "npm cache is not found" just means this was the first run, so the cache was saved here. That's harmless.
- The deprecation warnings come from the action, not your code. 0 vulnerabilities, and the token is read-only.
- The date is again today (13/10/2026), not last week. The paste again repeats the run several times and the last copy is cut off.

This third log (PR #5, 20:37 UTC) is clean on its own: 30/30 tests passed, nothing marked expected-fail, 0 vulnerabilities. The only issue is the same Node 20 / actions v4 deprecation as the other two. The paste is duplicated and cut off at the end again, and it's from today (13/10), not last week.

I checked GitHub against `main`, and that turned up the real worry:

- **PR #6 (tests) was merged on the 21:38 run, the one with 5 expected-fail tests.** So the merged PR passed CI while 5 tests were marked as known failures. Those failures probably point at real bugs in invoices or customers that are still there.
- **`main` doesn't contain any merged PR.** It has only 3 commits, ending at `61fc71a` (08:54 today). PR #2 and PR #4 (invoice totals fix) and PR #6 all show as merged after that, but none are in `main`. So `main` was force-pushed or reset after the merges. That also explains why PR #5's base (`7324522`) doesn't match.
- **The CSV export never landed.** PR #3 and PR #5 were both closed without merging.

In short, `main` has no invoice totals fix, no CSV export and no PR #6 tests. If you reset the sandbox on purpose, that's fine. If not, work is lost.

Options:
- **A**: task "Invoices: fix the bugs behind PR #6's expected-fail tests". A thread gets the tests back from PR #6's commit `26452b5`, fixes the code and makes every test truly pass.
- **B**: upgrade CI to Node 24 and actions v5.
- **C**: redo the work missing from `main`: the invoice totals fix ("Invoices:" title) and the CSV export.
- Any combination, or **Neither**.

I haven't created any task. I'm waiting for your choice.

Open questions: none.

I've queued the task "Invoices: Add PDF download for invoices" to start right away. It asks for:
- a "Download PDF" link for each invoice on `/invoices`
- a valid PDF with the date in DD/MM/YYYY, the line items and the total

The PDF reuses the same total calculation as the page, so the two always agree. The thread must also add tests and a changelog entry, run the app and click the link to check the download, then send back a working browser link.

One thing to know: the totals code (`Math.floor` in `lineTotalCents`) is probably where the off-by-one-cent bug lives, so the PDF will show the same totals the page does. I left that alone in this task, and option C would fix it.

Still waiting on A / B / C / Neither from the CI review.

{"title":"Invoices: Add PDF download for invoices","brief":"Owner request (13/10/2026 22:47): "Add a PDF download for invoices."

Outcome required: on the Invoices page, each invoice has a visible "Download PDF" link/button. Clicking it downloads a real, valid PDF of that invoice.

Current code:
- `src/web/server.ts` is a plain `node:http` server (port `PORT`, default 4173). `/invoices` (the default route) renders a table with one hardcoded invoice ("Invoice 1"). Its total comes from `invoiceTotalCents([{ quantity: 2, unitPrice: 12.50 }])`.
- `src/invoices/index.ts` exports `Line`, `lineTotalCents`, `invoiceTotalCents`, and `invoiceDate` (en-GB, so DD/MM/YYYY).

What to build:
1. Add a route, e.g. `GET /invoices/<id>.pdf` or `/invoices/<id>/pdf`, that responds with `Content-Type: application/pdf` and `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="invoice-<id>.pdf"`. Return 404 for an unknown id.
2. The PDF must contain at least:
   - invoice number/title
   - date in DD/MM/YYYY (project rule: dates are always DD/MM/YYYY; use `invoiceDate`)
   - line items (quantity, unit price, line total)
   - invoice total
   Totals must come from the same `src/invoices` functions the page uses, so the PDF and the page always agree. Do not duplicate the money maths. Note: `lineTotalCents` uses `Math.floor(unitPrice * 100)`, a known rounding concern. Do not change it in this task, but mention it in your report if it affects the PDF.
3. Refactor the hardcoded invoice data just enough that the page and the PDF route read the same invoice source.
4. Generating the PDF: a small well-maintained library (e.g. pdfkit) or a minimal hand-written PDF are both fine. Prefer robust and simple. Keep `npm ci` working, and avoid native build deps.
5. Tests: add vitest tests in `src/invoices` and/or `src/web` covering:
   - the PDF route status and headers
   - the response starting with `%PDF-`
   - the PDF containing the total and the DD/MM/YYYY date
   - the 404 case
6. CI (`.github/workflows/checks.yml`) runs `npm run lint` (tsc), `npm run check:changelog`, and `npm test` with TZ=UTC. All must pass, so add a changelog entry. No `.fails`/`skip`/`todo` tests.
7. E2E verification: start the app as a managed app with `jevellan_app_start`. Open `/invoices` in a browser, check the link looks right (pixel-tidy, no emoji), click it, and confirm the downloaded file opens as a PDF with the correct content.

Report back with:
- the route
- the library choice
- test results
- a description or screenshot of the PDF
- the verified browser link to the running app","type":"feature","goalId":null,"now":true,"after":[],"needs":[],"fixed":{},"source":"owner-request"}
